newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian president urges speed on hydrocarbons code.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian president urges speed on hydrocarbons code.

text.p: Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali on Thursday asked his government to speed up the issuing of a long-awaited hydrocarbons code aimed at giving more incentives for oil firms to invest in the country, officials said.
They said the call was made after a report on reforms in the energy sector presented to him by Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra.

Ben Ali also recommended the preparation of a programme for the restructuring of the energy distribution sector, they said. Last year the government was planning to sell off a minority stake in the state-run distributing firm AGIL.
Forty two oil firms are currently operating in Tunisia in 40 concessions. Tunisia this year granted international oil firms six new permits for exploration.
The North African country produced an estimated 4.3 milion tonnes of crude in 1996.
